universal_lens: Partition lattice structure under subpartition refinement and product operation generates a μ-partition hierarchy that, restricted to the interval algebra P of left-closed right-open intervals and its finite-disjoint-union closure R, yields the canonical semiring foundation for Lebesgue measure on ℝ.
gsi_mapping: Subpartition refinement maps to Bayesian evidence updating; partition product maps to joint likelihood factorization; μ-partition inheritance maps to conformal prediction set validity; interval algebra P maps to atomic hypothesis space; R maps to composite event sigma-algebra.

primitives.name: Subpartition Refinement Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: 8] If {E} and {Fj} are partitions of E, then {Ei} is called a subpartition of {Fj} if each set Ei is contained in one of the sets Fj.
primitives.assumptions: Partitions are finite collections of disjoint sets whose union equals E; underlying set E is arbitrary.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails for infinite partitions without σ-algebra structure; fails if containment is not measurable.

layer2.mapping: Subpartition refinement ≡ Bayesian evidence refinement: finer partition = more informative likelihood; GSI: posterior contraction over hypothesis partitions; GSE: information filtration for state estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Partition entropy reduction ΔH = H({F_j}) - H({E_i}) ≥ 0; conformal coverage validity under refinement.

primitives.name: Partition Product Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: (5a) If {E} and {Fj} are partitions of E, then so is their product, consisting of all sets of the form Éi ∩ Fj.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: E_i, F_j: dimensionless (set-theoretic); ⊗: binary operator on partition lattice
primitives.assumptions: Partitions are finite; intersection distributes over union; product partition remains finite.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Product cardinality explodes combinatorially; fails for non-disjoint generating sets; measure-theoretic product requires σ-finiteness.

layer2.mapping: Partition product ≡ joint likelihood factorization: GSI: product of independent evidence partitions yields joint posterior; GSE: transition kernel between state partitions via intersection of pre/post partitions.
layer2.telemetry: Product partition cardinality |{E_i}|·|{F_j}|; mutual information I({E_i};{F_j}) = H({E_i})+H({F_j})-H({E_i}⊗{F_j}).

primitives.name: μ-Partition Inheritance Axiom
primitives.verbatim_quote: (5b) If a subpartition of a partition {Ei} is a μ-partition, then {E} is a μ-partition.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{M}_\mu: dimensionless (collection of μ-partitions); μ: pre-measure on semiring P
primitives.assumptions: μ is a pre-measure on semiring P; μ-partition means partition sets are in P and μ-additivity holds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if μ is not countably additive; fails for non-measurable subpartitions; fails if pre-measure not defined on generating semiring.

layer2.mapping: μ-partition inheritance ≡ conformal calibration monotonicity: GSI: if refined partition is calibrated, coarser partition inherits validity; GSE: invariant measure propagates upward in information filtration.
layer2.telemetry: Calibration error bound ε({E_i}) ≤ ε({F_j}) for {E_i} ⪯ {F_j}; measure consistency μ(∪E_i) = Σμ(E_i).

primitives.name: Interval Algebra Foundation
primitives.verbatim_quote: We shall denote by P the class of all bounded, left closed, and right open intervals, i.e.
primitives.latex: \mathcal{P} = \{ [a,b) \mid a,b \in \mathbb{R}, a < b \\}, \quad \mathcal{R} = \{ \bigcup_{k=1}^n I_k \mid I_k \in \mathcal{P}, I_k \cap I_l = \emptyset \}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: a,b: length (meters); [a,b): dimensionless (set); Lebesgue measure λ([a,b)) = b-a (meters)
primitives.assumptions: Real line ℝ with standard topology; intervals are bounded; finite additivity on disjoint unions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Unbounded intervals require extension; countable unions require σ-algebra completion; non-measurable sets (Vitali) break λ-additivity.

layer2.mapping: P = atomic state space for GSE situational reasoning; R = composite state space; λ = invariant measure for Bayesian updating in GSI; partition product on P generates transition kernel for state evolution.
layer2.telemetry: Lebesgue measure λ on P; outer measure λ* on ℝ; Carathéodory extension to Borel σ-algebra; conformal prediction interval coverage.

The four primitives form a complete algebraic hierarchy: (1) Subpartition operator defines a partial order on partitions, inducing an information filtration. (2) Partition product provides a meet operation in the partition lattice, corresponding to joint evidence combination. (3) μ-partition inheritance ensures measure-theoretic consistency propagates upward along the filtration, guaranteeing that calibration at fine resolution implies calibration at coarse resolution. (4) Interval algebra P and its finite-disjoint-union closure R instantiate this abstract hierarchy on ℝ, with Lebesgue pre-measure λ([a,b)) = b-a providing the quantitative measure. The product of partitions on P generates the semiring structure necessary for Carathéodory extension. Failure modes: combinatorial explosion of product partitions requires σ-finiteness for infinite extensions; non-measurable subpartitions break inheritance; unbounded intervals require compactification. The duality between partition refinement (information gain) and measure additivity (probability conservation) is the core structural unification.
